ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Read the three inequalities in the problem statement: x-y+3≥0, x+y+1≥0, x≤k. First simplify them separately: from x-y+3≥0, obtain y≤x+3; from x+y+1≥0, obtain y≥-x-1; the third remains x≤k. To simultaneously satisfy the first two restrictions on y, the lower bound must not exceed the upper bound, that is, -x-1≤x+3. Solving gives -4≤2x, so x≥-2. Therefore the feasible region in the x direction must satisfy -2≤x≤k. If the feasible region is nonempty, then k≥-2 is necessary; when k=-2, the feasible region degenerates into the point (-2,1); when k>-2, the three vertices of the feasible region are the intersection point of the two slanted lines (-2,1), and the intersection points of the line x=k with y=x+3 and y=-x-1, namely (k,k+3), (k,-k-1).
